documentation.subject: ${SERVICE_NAME}: the database is slow or refusing work
documentation.content:
Either the readiness probe is taking longer than half a second, or the Prisma client is raising errors at a sustained rate. Both are the shape of connection-pool exhaustion, a sleeping or overloaded branch, or a provider incident.

This is only half of the database signal. Connection-count and storage quotas belong to the database provider and are not visible from this project — the other half is an alert configured in the provider's own console. See `docs/20-deployment-observability.md` section 5.

Runbook: `docs/ops/deployment-runbooks.md`, "The database is slow or refusing connections".

First three commands:

    gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="${SERVICE_NAME}" AND jsonPayload.event="readiness_check_slow"' --freshness 1h --limit 20 --format='value(timestamp,jsonPayload.latencyMs)'
    gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="${SERVICE_NAME}" AND jsonPayload.errorClass=~"^Prisma"' --freshness 1h --limit 30 --format='value(timestamp,jsonPayload.event,jsonPayload.errorClass)'
    curl -sS "$(gcloud run services describe ${SERVICE_NAME} --region europe-west3 --format='value(status.url)')/v1/health/ready"

Stop condition: `PrismaClientInitializationError` means the connection string or the pooler is wrong and no amount of waiting fixes it. `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` at a low rate around a deploy or a shutdown is the pool closing and is not an incident.
